newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed near session highs on Monday, bouncing back after Friday's 7.96 point AEX sell off, although dealers said volumes were light and today's action reflected lack of selling as much as anything.
"This just corrects the fall which we had on Friday," said one dealer. "The market has a positive stance today on the back off the dollar but with hardly any volume," said another.

The AEX index of leading Dutch shares closed 3.99 points up at 554.98 but dealers said volumes had been slack all day and notably thin in the afternoon due to the absence of the Wall Street market, closed for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
Chartists' opinion is divided over whether the market is going to climb once it breaks out of its current doldrums or fall back through current support levels.

"Current market technicals, indicating that the general shrot term trend is down, express a short term selling condition," ING Barings said in an investment note. "Current chart readings suggest that the downward trend may continue for a while. We expect a weak market in the next few weeks..."
In contrast Fibonacci Press sees the market gaining. "The intermediate term trend is still up," it said. "Some backing and filling will be needed before the uptrend resumes."
Dealers said lingering concerns about the next move in interest rates were keeping some out of the market although new money was seen coming in during the first weeks of September.
"Its a new month and some investments have to be made before the end of the quarter," said a dealer. "My clients are not fully invested and they're waiting for opportunities."

One such could be the restructuring at Unilever mooted in two newspaper interviews with the new UK chairman Niall FitzGerald, the dealer said. FitzGerald told Britain's Sunday Times and the Wall Street Journal that the sprawling Unilever business needed to be pruned back aggressively to flourish.

Unilever closed 4.40 guilders up at 242.90 on the articles. "People have been looking for this thing from Unilever for a long time," said an analyst. "People would dearly love to see the company really focusing on what's important to it."
One dealer said hard evidence of a restructuring could unlock something like 10 percent of the value of Unilever, giving the share a 260-guilder target price.

"Unilever could look at 260 a share but we need proof of the restructuring. We've been waiting for years -- if we see some more proof and some divestments that will push the shares up and there's a very nice 10 percent hidden in the current price."

Royal Dutch closed 3.90 guilders higher at 251.90, pushing up in line with the oil price in reaction to fresh Iraqi/Kurdish tensions. "The only threat the United Nations has realistically is to block the oil-for-food deal with Iraq, which would affect (oil) inventories down the line," said a dealer.

Elsewhere among the leaders moves were modest with Philips up 10 cents to 56.20 guilders, KLM 70 cents higher at 46.40 guilders and Aegon up the same amount to 81.70 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
